data.executive_summary:
Imagur’s public image-sharing site (Imager at imagesharer.xyz) was assessed on 18 September 2026 with the owner’s authorization.

Imagur is a public image-sharing web application branded “Imager — your images, your control.” The service runs PHP/nginx on imagesharer.xyz and offers login, register, dashboard, image upload (private/public), and profile avatars.

This assessment confirmed **14 findings: 2 critical, 2 high, 4 medium, 5 low, and 1 informational.**

The most serious issues are that customer image files sit in an Amazon S3 bucket that anyone can list and download — including images marked private — and that AWS keys used for that storage appear in a public JavaScript file. A logged-in user can also place an image into another customer’s account, and a crafted filename can run script in visitors’ browsers. Session cookies and forms are weakly protected, and the database and extra web ports are visible on the internet.

**Highest-priority actions**

1. Lock the S3 bucket.
2. Rotate and remove the published AWS keys.
3. Bind uploads to the logged-in user on the server.
4. Encode filenames.

**Findings at a glance**

| Severity | Title |
|:---|:---|
| Critical | Public S3 bucket lists and serves private images |
| Critical | AWS access keys published in public JavaScript |
| High | Upload form trusts client-supplied user_id (IDOR) |
| High | Stored cross-site scripting via image filename |
| Medium | Session cookie missing Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite |
| Medium | No CSRF protection on account and upload actions |
| Medium | PostgreSQL reachable on the public internet |
| Medium | SQL errors disclose database and source-file details |
| Low | SSH allows password logins from the internet |
| Low | Extra Apache site on port 8080 |
| Low | HTTPS directories redirect to HTTP |
| Low | www hostname certificate name mismatch |
| Low | CloudFront hostname uses the wrong TLS certificate |
| Info | Server and framework versions leaked |

data.scope:
Authorized, non-destructive full-scope web and origin assessment of Imagur (public brand: Imager). Testing was limited to owner-approved assets. Neighboring cloud customers and lookalike domains were excluded.

**In-scope (owner-approved)**

| System | Description |
|:---|:---|
| imagesharer.xyz (http and https) | Main Imager website |
| www.imagesharer.xyz | Same site as the main website |
| resources.imagesharer.xyz | Imagur CloudFront hostname |
| d273uevi0662l0.cloudfront.net | CloudFront distribution hostname for this Imagur distribution only |
| 51.161.131.44 | Origin IP only as the host of the website (not neighboring OVH customers) |
| S3 bucket filesharer-research | Discovered through the in-scope upload feature; tested only as Imagur image storage. Other customers’ objects were not downloaded |

**Out of scope**

| System | Description |
|:---|:---|
| imagur.xyz, imager.xyz, imagesharer.net, fshare.xyz | Lookalike / related domains excluded after owner scope choice |
| imgur.com, fshare.vn | Unrelated third-party brands |
| Flinders University | Third party |
| Google | Third party |
| Spaceship/Cloudflare shared DNS | Shared platforms |
| OVH netblock except 51.161.131.44 | Other customers on the same provider |
| CloudFront co-tenants | Shared CDN platform |
| AWS account APIs | No use of leaked AWS secrets against the AWS account APIs |

**Methodology**

Authorized, non-destructive full-scope web and origin assessment. Fast port probe then version scan of open ports only. Authenticated testing via public self-registration of two assessment accounts. Manual verification of upload, IDOR, XSS, storage, cookies, and TLS. No DDoS, malware, phishing, credential stuffing, password spraying, brute force, or destructive techniques.
data.provided_users:
No production customer accounts were supplied by the owner.

Authenticated testing used two assessment accounts created through the public self-registration page on imagesharer.xyz.

Password authentication on SSH and PostgreSQL was not brute-forced.

list_of_changes.description: Initial report of the authorized assessment completed on 18 September 2026.

appendix_sections.title: Coverage
appendix_sections.content:
The following areas were covered during the 18 September 2026 assessment:

* Origin 51.161.131.44 ports 22, 80, 443, 5432, 8080
* Unauthenticated and authenticated Imager app (login, register, dashboard, profile, upload, avatars, JSON API)
* CloudFront resources hostname
* Application S3 storage for images

appendix_sections.title: Limitations
appendix_sections.content:
* Password authentication on SSH/PostgreSQL was not brute-forced.
* Leaked AWS secret was not used to call AWS APIs; access-key id match to production S3 URLs was used as attribution.
* S3 listing showed other keys; those objects were not retrieved.
* Candidate lookalike domains were excluded after owner scope choice.
* No phone number on file.
